messages:
oncall-bot: @channel Hotseat handoff: primary -> sophie (hotseat) | secondary -> andre. Please confirm coverage and surface any in-flight mitigations. Incident queue: 3 active pagers.

sophie: taking hotseat now. leaving quick notes below — short checklist first, then runbook links + commands. tagging @andre @mike for gaps. :wave:

andre: ack. I'm secondary but on a 1hr call in 15m — will be reachable via DM for urgent pages.

mike: ping — which services have elevated error rates? I can do KV-cache fallback if needed.

ops-bot: Incident alert summary (last 30m):
- inference-api: increased 5xxs from model-pool-a (p99 latency spike)
- embed-worker: queue depth up x3 (backpressure)
- routing-proxy: incident rate 1.2% (threshold 0.5%)

sophie: customer-impact quick map:
- high: hosted API customers on model-pool-a (real-time chat flows) — may see timeouts and 5xxs.
- medium: dedicated customers with autoscale enabled — may see throttling until new nodes warm.
- low: embeddings pipelines — slower throughput but not failing.

sophie: hotseat checklist (do this first)
1) Confirm primary/secondary contact details + timezone (done).
2) Check incidentbot runbook hits and active playbooks.
3) Verify KV cache KV nodes in pool (if p99 latency suggests KV thrash).
4) If model-pool resource starved, promote compatible fallback model variant.
5) Open P0 ticket if any customer-facing SLOs breached -> notify success.

sophie: runbook quick-links (internal):
- KV cache fallback: https://runbooks.internal/kv-cache-fallback
- Model fallback & rollout: https://runbooks.internal/model-fallback-rollout
- Routing proxy rollback: https://runbooks.internal/routing-proxy-rollback
- Incident triage template: https://runbooks.internal/incident-triage-template

andre: adding a note — if you go KV-fallback, remember to set the flag on the canary first:
```
# flip canary for kv fallback
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://admin.internal/flags/kv_fallback -d '{"state":"on","scope":"canary"}'
```

mike: if model fallback needed, prefer the quantized-2 variant (faster warmup). Steps I use:
- scale up 2x instances on model-pool-b
- set route policy: fallback -> quantized-2 (5% canary)
- monitor p95/p99 for 10 minutes then increase to 50%

sophie: shortcut commands I keep in my pocket for this hotseat:
- check failing pods: `kubectl -n inference get pods --selector=app=model-pool-a`
- tail logs for 1 pod: `kubectl -n inference logs -f pod/model-a-xxxx`
- dump recent 5xxs: `jq '.status' /var/logs/api/requests.log | grep 5.. | wc -l`

lia: small nit — embedding queue backlog increase usually follows proxy timeouts; watch the worker backoff metrics: `embed.worker.backoff.count`

sophie: quick mitigation priority order (what I'll do first if pages spike)
A) short-term: toggle routing-proxy read-timeout to 6s to allow retries (see rollback snippet below).
B) mid-term: flip kv cache fallback for affected model-pool.
C) mid/long-term: promote quantized variant and scale dedicated nodes.

sophie: routing-proxy toggle (use with caution):
```
# temp bump of read timeout to absorb transient slowness
curl -X PATCH https://admin.internal/proxy-config \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"readTimeoutMs":6000}'
```

andre: if you do A, add a note in the incident ticket that we changed timeouts and will revert after stabilization. Remind ops to expect increased tail latency on the dashboard.

mike: I'll standby to push model fallback if we confirm resource starvation. also happy to pair on the canary rollout.

sophie: leaving two quick scripts below for rapid rollback and canary check. copy/paste usable in shell.
```
# check canary status
HTTP_STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://canary.internal/health)
if [ "$HTTP_STATUS" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "canary unhealthy, aborting rollout"
  exit 1
fi
# rollback routing proxy
kubectl -n infra set image deploy/routing-proxy routing-proxy=registry/redwood/routing-proxy:stable
```

oncall-bot: @sophie Pager assigned: primary (hotseat). Summary: routing-proxy and inference-api alerts active. Use `/incident create` to open P0 if SLOs breached.

lia: FYI — customer success flagged a major customer convo thread hitting 504s; might need priority comms if we escalate. I'll open a CS ping.

andre: coverage gap: I'm offline for 1hr starting 5320001250 (call). sophie, if you need me during that window DM escalate -> @mike can take over secondary if needed.

sophie: noted. @mike will be temporary secondary 5320001250-5320001550 if @andre unreachable. I'll update the bridge topic and incident ticket.

mike: ack. I'll watch the metrics dashboard and be ready to run fallback playbooks.

sophie: final handoff notes before I go grab coffee — leaving breadcrumbs in ticket:
- actions done: increased proxy readTimeout -> 6000ms at 5320001240, started canary check 5320001246
- next actions: if p95 remains > 1.5s after 10min -> trigger model fallback canary 5% (ops runbook link above)
- comms: CS notified; will draft status update if we promote to P0.

sophie: ping me in #oncall-dms for anything urgent. leaving the bridge open. :coffee:

oncall-bot: Bridge created: https://meet.internal/bridge/5320001234. Logs and traces auto-attached to incident ticket #INC-5321.

mike: quick reminder to add `reason=timeout-spike` when flipping flags so we have structured logging for audit.

sophie: good call. I'll add that to the ticket. dropping a short checklist message in the ticket now.

mike: 👍

(END OF THREAD)
